title: Rhoda at the gate (Acts 12:1–17)
hookLine: Peter escapes prison, and the maid is so glad she forgets to open the door

cards: It's the middle of the night in Jerusalem, and a house is full of people praying. They have reason to. King Herod has just killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
And now Herod has arrested Peter, and plans to bring him out after the feast. So the church prays for him, hard, all night. Then someone knocks at the outer gate.
And what happens next comes close to comedy.

teach.b: First, the prison. Peter is asleep between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with guards at the door. An angel appears, light fills the cell, and the angel strikes Peter on the side: get up, quickly.
The chains fall off. Put on your shoes, wrap your cloak, follow me. Peter thinks he's dreaming.
They pass the first guard and the second, and the iron gate to the city opens by itself. Then the angel is gone, and Peter, alone in the street, realizes it's real.
He goes to the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, where the church is praying, and knocks. A servant girl named Rhoda comes to answer.

teach.h: SHE OPENED NOT THE GATE FOR JOY.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "as soon as she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for joy." She runs inside to tell everyone and leaves him standing in the street. And the people praying for his release?
They tell her she's out of her mind. She insists.

teach.h: THOU ART MAD. IT IS HIS ANGEL.
teach.b: Then it must be his angel, they say.

Meanwhile, the text says, "Peter continued knocking." Finally they open, and they are astonished. Peter waves them quiet, tells them how the Lord brought him out, and says: tell these things to James, and to the brethren.
Then he leaves for another place. Luke doesn't hide how slow the praying church was to believe its own prayer had been answered. And the one who believed first was the servant at the door.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saints Peter and Paul on June 29, and this reading of Peter's release from prison is the first reading at that day's Mass.

the angel who led Peter out of the prison
the servant girl who heard Peter at the gate

games.q: you're Rhoda. it's the middle of the night and you hear Peter's voice at the gate. what do you do?
o: ask who it is to be sure.
games.why: she's so glad she runs in to tell them and forgets to open. Peter keeps knocking while they argue with her.

practice: Think back over a year or two: was there something you hoped or prayed for that actually came, a job, a phone call, a reconciliation, and you barely noticed?
Maybe you were slow to believe it, like the room that told Rhoda she was mad; let yourself smile at that, because her mistake was joy and theirs was doubt, and either way Peter got in.
If you pray, say thank you for one thing you forgot to thank God for.

wordCard.voice: Rhoda. The servant girl so glad to hear Peter's voice that she forgot to let him in, and believed before anyone else did. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: Rhoda, a name from the Greek word for rose. the servant girl who heard Peter's voice.

carryVoice: Your line: she forgot to open. That's week seventy-eight: if it be of God, deacon, Ethiopian, brother, Tabitha, Christian, and Rhoda at the gate. Day five hundred forty-six, done.
